title: Add median-slope invocation metrics and SLO trajectory explorer (alert tuning wizard)
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add median-slope metrics to help detect gradual latency/cost drift; introduce an SLO Trajectory Explorer dashboard and Alert Tuning Wizard to calibrate hysteresis and decay for token-level SLOs.
description:
Context: We see frequent noisy alert churn driven by slow, sustained drifts in per-invocation latency and token-cost rather than short spikes. Root cause analysis often required manual trend-fitting across windows.
Motivation: provide a first-class metric that captures the slope (direction + magnitude) of key invocation signals and give operators a guided UI to visualize SLO trajectory, simulate alert behavior, and generate tuned alert rules.
What this PR does:
1) Adds a new metric family (invocation.median_slope.{latency_ms,token_cost}) which computes a robust median-of-window slopes per route and per model-variant with labels for phase_bucket (init, prefix, steady), tenant, region. The implementation uses a sliding-window median-of-deltas to reduce sensitivity to transient spikes.
2) Introduces a small synthetic baseline generator and replaybench (examples/synthetic-baselines/replaybench.py) used by the dashboard's simulation panels so teams can predict alert noise under different drift scenarios.
3) Adds an SLO Trajectory Explorer dashboard (dashboards/slo_trajectory_explorer.json) which surfaces: time-series of slope metrics, drift heatmap by tenant, simulated alert firings for candidate thresholds and hysteresis, and a recommended rule snippet.
4) Includes an Alert Tuning Wizard (docs/observability/alerting-wizard.md + runbooks/slo-trajectory.md) with operational guidance, decision trees, and links to Linear tickets for staged rollout.
5) Exposes telemetry labels and small runtime config knobs to enable/disable slope computation per deployment to keep overhead minimal.
Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive; no existing metrics were removed.
Overhead: end-to-end internal benchmark on a medium traffic trace showed ~3.2% CPU on a single auth shard with slope window=5m, sampling=1s (details in tests/bench_results.md).
Checklist:
- [x] Implementation and unit tests for slope aggregator - tests/slope_sampler_test.go
- [x] Dashboard JSON and example notebooks - dashboards/slo_trajectory_explorer.json
- [x] Runbook and alert playbook - runbooks/slo-trajectory.md
- [x] Integration test using synthetic replaybench - examples/synthetic-baselines/replaybench.py
- [x] Feature-flagged via config: observability.slope.enabled (default true in hosted)
Migration notes: Add the new metrics to Datadog/Prometheus scrape config; dashboards reference label phase_bucket which will be present for instrumented routes.
Rollout plan: canary on observability-stage for 48h, collect overhead metrics and false-positive counts, then broad rollouts by region.

CI: Initial CI run failed on lint (line-length in README snippet) and a flaky test in bench harness. I addressed lint and stabilized the harness (use deterministic RNG seed). Final CI: all checks passed — unit, bench, integration, linters, rollout-sim smoke.
Review conversation summary:
- Marco Ruiz (reviewer): "Nice approach to slope stabilization. Two asks: (1) can we expose a percentile-based slope (p90) for tenants with high variance? (2) please add an explicit cost estimate per 100k invocations to the runbook." — Author reply: "(1) I added a TODO and small extension point in slope_sampler.go to allow percentile aggregation; will follow up in a dedicated PR to avoid scope creep. (2) Added cost estimate section to runbooks/slo-trajectory.md with numbers from the bench run."
- Priya Shah (reviewer): "Dashboard looks great. Request: make the simulated alert preview include alert-silence windows so teams can test maintenance windows." — Author reply: "Added simulated silence support and a toggle in the dashboard JSON; also documented in alerting-wizard.md."
- Omar El-Gamal (approver): "Approve after CI green. Verify that default flags are safe for on-prem (disabled by default in the installer)." — Author reply: "Verified; installer default for private is false; docs updated."
Post-merge ops: I created a Linear story (ENG-2127) to track the follow-up PR for percentile-slope and another (ENG-2199) for telemetry exporters. I also added an item to the runbook to run a 7-day canary analysis and file SUP-4432 if false-positive rate exceeds 10% in any tenant.
Notes for on-call:
- If slope metrics suddenly spike for many tenants, check kernel queue/backpressure metrics first (observability/kernel_queue).
- Use replaybench to reproduce noisy drift locally.
- To temporarily silence noisy alerts, use the Alert Tuning Wizard’s suggested hysteresis of 3 windows + 10% decay.
Why this is different: Rather than only surfacing raw delta or percent-change, median-of-window slopes give robust drift detection for slow degradations, and the explorer couples live telemetry with a simulation loop so SREs can see how changes to hysteresis/decay affect future alert churn.
